newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rebound in technical correction.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rebound in technical correction.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Tuesday as a corrective rebound put a stop to the downward slide in recent sessions.

Traders said there were some shorts in the market which helped carry prices higher early on. But the market dropped from its mid-session highs as U.S. Treasuries eased in the afternoon, one trader said.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/2 to 89-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.25 to 125.75.

Traders did not think this session's respite was likely to continue, considering that U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan is set to give testimony to Congress again Wednesday and key U.S. unemployment figures are due Friday.
"The market is heading a little lower," said the trader.
"Latin Bradies are mostly higher but the tone is cautious. Look for one more downside thrust to recent lows before a potential bottom develops," said MMS International in an investor note.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.0 percent from 5.75 percent.
